## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Khantivaṇṇajātaka* (Ja 225) is a narrative included in the Jātaka collection of the Pali canon [SuttaCentral]. According to the traditional introductory narrative (*paccuppannavatthu*), the Buddha recounted the story at Jetavana regarding the King of Kosala [SuttaCentral]. A highly competent subordinate in the royal service had engaged in an intrigue within the king's harem; nevertheless, acknowledging the official's usefulness, the king chose to bear the insult with forbearance and reported the situation to the Buddha [SuttaCentral]. In response, the Buddha noted that rulers in ancient times had acted likewise and narrated the tale of the past (*atītavatthu*) [SuttaCentral].
